grammar.title: A tendency, not a rule for everyone
grammar.formation: Verb plain nonpast/i-adjective + ものだ; na-adjective + なものだ. Negative norms often use verb dictionary form + ものではない.
grammar.explanation: This use of ものだ presents a tendency or norm from the speaker’s viewpoint: unfamiliar places can feel confusing. It is not a measured claim about everyone. A personal past habit uses たものだ, a different use; an emotional exclamation also needs its own context. Here the generalisation is then applied to a concrete first-day experience.
grammar.example: 初めての場所では、戸惑うものだ。
grammar.translation: It’s natural to feel unsure in a place you haven’t been before.

examples.ja: {初|はじ}めての{場所|ばしょ}では、{戸惑|とまど}うものだ。
examples.en: It’s natural to feel unsure in a place you haven’t been before.

examples.ja: {自分|じぶん}の{間違|まちが}いは{気|き}づきにくいものだ。
examples.en: Your own mistakes can be hard to notice.

examples.ja: {人|ひと}の{話|はなし}を{途中|とちゅう}で{決|き}めつけるものではない。
examples.en: You shouldn’t jump to conclusions partway through someone’s explanation.

grammar.mistake: Do not read ものだ as a guarantee that every individual behaves this way. Do not use the recollection meaning of たものだ to answer a question about a general tendency.

grammar.title: Requested advice from someone with experience
grammar.formation: Verb dictionary form or ない-form + ことだ. Polite ending ことです is possible; it still gives a recommendation.
grammar.explanation: ことだ presents what the speaker regards as the appropriate thing to do for the stated goal. It can sound firm or authoritative. Ren gives advice after Kenta asks him for help; it is not a default way to order a teacher or supervisor about. This retrieves the advisory use introduced earlier, distinct from the noun こと and emotional expressions ending in ことだ.
grammar.example: 早く慣れたいなら、分からないことを聞くことだ。
grammar.translation: If you want to settle in quickly, ask about what you don’t understand.

examples.ja: {早|はや}く{慣|な}れたいなら、{分|わ}からないことを{聞|き}くことだ。
examples.en: If you want to settle in quickly, ask about what you don’t understand.

examples.ja: {一人|ひとり}で{抱|かか}え{込|こ}まないことだ。
examples.en: My advice is not to take everything on yourself.

examples.en: To prepare for the interview, first organise your own experiences.

grammar.mistake: Attach the plain dictionary or negative form, not 聞きますことだ. A polite ending does not remove the authoritative nuance; consider the listener and relationship.

grammar.title: Correct an inference without saying the opposite
grammar.formation: Verb/i-adjective plain form + わけではない; na-adjective + なわけではない. To quote a noun proposition, use Nだというわけではない. Casual ending わけじゃない.
grammar.explanation: The speaker rejects a proposed conclusion: asking for help does not mean abandoning responsibility. This need not assert the complete opposite, and it does not mean “impossible,” as わけがない does. Notice the scope of the statement being denied; 全部…わけではない often denies “all,” not “none.” Noun attachments also include の/である in appropriate attributive contexts; the quoted だという pattern here makes the intended proposition explicit.
grammar.example: 質問したからといって、何も分かっていないわけではない。
grammar.translation: Asking a question doesn’t mean you understand nothing.

examples.ja: {質問|しつもん}したからといって、{何|なに}も{分|わ}かっていないわけではない。
examples.en: Asking a question doesn’t mean you understand nothing.

examples.ja: {映画|えいが}が{嫌|きら}いなわけじゃないよ。
examples.en: It’s not that I dislike going to the movies.

examples.ja: {一人|ひとり}で{作業|さぎょう}する{人|ひと}が、{全員|ぜんいん}{専門|せんもん}{家|か}だというわけではない。
examples.en: Not everyone who works alone is an expert.

grammar.mistake: Do not swap わけではない with わけがない. The first rejects an inference; the second can express impossibility or strong disbelief.

grammar.title: A commitment prevents an action; a negative verb reverses it
grammar.formation: Verb dictionary form + わけにはいかない: cannot do it under the circumstances. Verb ない-form + わけにはいかない: cannot avoid doing it. Polite ending わけにはいきません.
grammar.explanation: This pattern describes an action the speaker cannot reasonably take because of an obligation or circumstances, even if physically possible. Leaving a promised draft unfinished differs from being unable to walk out. With ない, the meaning reverses: 確認しないわけにはいかない means the speaker has to check. Read the first verb before deciding whether the action is blocked or required.
grammar.example: 今日は担当なので、先に帰るわけにはいかない。
grammar.translation: I’m responsible today, so I can’t just go home first.

examples.ja: {今日|きょう}は{担当|たんとう}なので、{先|さき}に{帰|かえ}るわけにはいかない。
examples.en: I’m responsible today, so I can’t just go home first.

examples.ja: {約束|やくそく}したから、{校正|こうせい}をしないわけにはいかない。
examples.en: I promised, so I have to proofread it.

examples.ja: {借|か}りた{本|ほん}なので、{人|ひと}に{貸|か}すわけにはいきません。
examples.en: It’s a borrowed book, so I can’t lend it to someone else.

grammar.mistake: 忘れるわけにはいかない forbids forgetting; 忘れないわけにはいかない would say forgetting is unavoidable. Never ignore the negative before わけ.

dialogues.title: A first shift is not a test of doing everything alone
dialogues.scene: After a first shift, Kenta asks Ren how to deal with questions he could not answer. Ren recalls his own first day. Kenta decides to ask the supervisor about the till at tomorrow’s meeting before the shop opens.

readings.title: Change the screening, keep the promise
paragraphs: {木曜日|もくようび}の{午後|ごご}、{友人|ゆうじん}に{映画|えいが}に{誘|さそ}われた。{前|まえ}から{気|き}になっていた{作品|さくひん}だが、{私|わたし}は{地域|ちいき}の{新聞|しんぶん}に{載|の}せる{記事|きじ}の{草稿|そうこう}を{直|なお}していた。{題名|だいめい}は{決|き}まり、{本文|ほんぶん}には{取材|しゅざい}した{二人|ふたり}のコメントも{入|はい}っている。しかし、{数字|すうじ}と{名前|なまえ}の{校正|こうせい}はまだ{終|お}わっていなかった。

{掲載|けいさい}は{月曜日|げつようび}だが、{推敲|すいこう}を{終|お}えた{記事|きじ}は{木曜日|もくようび}の{五時|ごじ}までに{送|おく}る{約束|やくそく}である。{金曜日|きんようび}には{紙面|しめん}を{作|つく}るので、その{時間|じかん}も{必要|ひつよう}なのだ。{月曜日|げつようび}まで{余裕|よゆう}があるというわけではない。{私|わたし}が{遅|おく}れると、{他|ほか}の{人|ひと}の{作業|さぎょう}まで{遅|おく}れてしまう。{途中|とちゅう}で{映画|えいが}に{行|い}くわけにはいかなかった。

{友人|ゆうじん}にそう{話|はな}すと、{翌日|よくじつ}の{六時|ろくじ}の{回|かい}を{提案|ていあん}してくれた。{私|わたし}は{映画|えいが}そのものを{断念|だんねん}したいわけではない。{金曜日|きんようび}に{行|い}けば、{心残|こころのこ}りなく{楽|たの}しめる。その{日|ひ}は{確認|かくにん}を{怠|おこた}らず、{名前|なまえ}の{表記|ひょうき}を{取材|しゅざい}のメモと{比|くら}べた。{約束|やくそく}したから、{最後|さいご}まで{確認|かくにん}しないわけにはいかなかった。

{責任感|せきにんかん}がある{人|ひと}は、{決|けっ}して{予定|よてい}を{変|か}えない。そう{一概|いちがい}に{言|い}えるだろうか。{急|きゅう}な{事情|じじょう}で{間|ま}に{合|あ}わないと{分|わ}かったら、{黙|だま}って{遅|おく}れるより、{早|はや}めに{相談|そうだん}した{方|ほう}がよいと{私|わたし}は{思|おも}う。{今回|こんかい}は{作業|さぎょう}を{終|お}える{見込|みこ}みがあったので、{元|もと}の{約束|やくそく}を{守|まも}った。{映画|えいが}を{見|み}たい{気持|きも}ちも、{記事|きじ}を{仕上|しあ}げる{決意|けつい}も、どちらも{変|か}わっていない。

exercises.prompt: When does Kenta decide to ask about the till?
options: At tomorrow’s meeting before the shop opens
After tomorrow’s customers form a queue
Only after Ren has left the shop
exercises.explain: Ren suggests the pre-opening meeting, and Kenta says he could ask then.

options: A button he had learned the day before
The title of Bao’s newspaper article
A promise to book cinema seats
exercises.explain: His memory is 前日に習ったボタン, and the following day he forgot it.

exercises.prompt: Which part of Ren’s advice had Kenta already followed that day?
options: Making a note of what he didn’t understand
Asking the manager before opening
Thanking Ren at the shop’s till
exercises.explain: Kenta says 今日のことはメモしたよ before they discuss when to ask.

exercises.context: Form practice: choose the taught expression of a common tendency, not a recommendation to feel confused.
exercises.line: {初|はじ}めての{場所|ばしょ}では、{戸惑|とまど}う＿＿。
options: ものだ
ことだ
わけがない
exercises.explain: ものだ presents the tendency. Advisory ことだ would recommend the action, and わけがない denies its possibility.

exercises.context: Form practice: use the plain verb before advisory ことだ.
exercises.line: {早|はや}く{慣|な}れたいなら、{分|わ}からないことを＿＿ことだ。
options: {聞|き}く
{聞|き}きます
{聞|き}いて
exercises.explain: Advisory ことだ attaches to the dictionary form 聞く. This explicitly tests formation.

exercises.context: Reply casually to Ren. You accept his suggestion to ask the manager at the meeting tomorrow morning.
exercises.line: {明日|あした}、{開店|かいてん}{前|まえ}に{店長|てんちょう}に{聞|き}いてみたら。
options: うん。メモを{見|み}せて、{聞|き}いてみるよ。
うん。{明日|あした}は{誰|だれ}にも{聞|き}かないことにするよ。
ううん。{映画|えいが}の{予約|よやく}はレンに{任|まか}せるよ。
exercises.explain: Showing the notes and asking implements the proposal. The others reject it or switch to an unrelated subject.

exercises.meaning: If you’re unsure, my advice is not to keep everything to yourself.
exercises.explain: The negative verb before ことだ advises against taking everything on alone.

exercises.prompt: What made the queue longer on the first day?
options: The writer kept trying to work it out alone
The manager required every customer to take notes
The writer asked the manager before opening
exercises.explain: The first paragraph explicitly links thinking alone with the growing queue.

exercises.prompt: What did the writer put in the notebook after talking to their brother?
options: Three questions
A complete list of every rule at the shop
A request to cancel the next shift
exercises.explain: They changed their plan for a long list and wrote three questions first.

exercises.prompt: What did the writer do differently the next afternoon?
options: Asked for help earlier when the same problem occurred
Avoided the till by leaving before work started
Spent longer trying to solve it alone
exercises.explain: The third paragraph says 今度は早めに声をかけた.

options: Friday at six
Thursday at four thirty
Monday at five
exercises.explain: They switch from today’s four-thirty film to tomorrow’s six o’clock showing; the scene is Thursday.

exercises.prompt: Why can’t Bao go out for the first screening?
options: He promised to finish and send the revision by five
Yamamoto said he must never go to films
Misaki has already bought seats for Monday
exercises.explain: He has a Thursday-five commitment; Monday is publication day.

exercises.prompt: What still needs checking after adding the comments?
options: The text, including its numbers
Whether a title has been chosen at all
Whether the comments have ever been added
exercises.explain: The title is decided and comments are added. Final proofreading and checking numbers remain.

exercises.context: Form practice: complete the na-adjective attachment before わけじゃない.
exercises.line: {映画|えいが}が{嫌|きら}い＿＿わけじゃないよ。
options: な
だ
に
exercises.explain: 嫌い is a na-adjective and uses 嫌いなわけじゃない in this attributive form.

exercises.context: Form practice: Bao must check the names because he promised. Choose the verb form that makes checking unavoidable.
exercises.line: {約束|やくそく}したから、{名前|なまえ}を＿＿わけにはいかない。
options: {確認|かくにん}しない
{確認|かくにん}する
{確認|かくにん}します
exercises.explain: 確認しないわけにはいかない means he has to check. 確認するわけにはいかない would block checking.

exercises.context: Reply casually to Misaki. Accept Friday’s six o’clock showing and explain that you’ll finish the draft first.
exercises.line: {明日|あした}の{六時|ろくじ}もあるよ。{私|わたし}はそっちでもいい。
options: ありがとう。{草稿|そうこう}を{出|だ}してから、{明日|あした}{行|い}こう。
ありがとう。{今日|きょう}の{四時半|よじはん}に{行|い}こう。
ううん。{映画|えいが}は{嫌|きら}いだから、もう{誘|さそ}わないで。
exercises.explain: The first accepts the proposed alternative and matches Bao’s plan. The other replies change the time or contradict his stated interest.

exercises.meaning: I promised, so I can’t go out leaving the draft unfinished.
tiles: {出|で}かけるわけにはいかない。
exercises.explain: The commitment blocks leaving. A positive dictionary verb before わけにはいかない has the opposite polarity to ないわけにはいかない.

exercises.prompt: Why isn’t Monday’s publication date enough to postpone the revision?
options: Other people need Friday for page layout
The newsletter is actually published Thursday afternoon
The cinema closes before Monday
exercises.explain: The second paragraph explains Friday’s layout step and its required time.

exercises.prompt: What does changing the screening show about the writer’s intention?
options: They still want to see the film after finishing the article
They have given up on watching the film altogether
They no longer intend to finish the article
exercises.explain: The third and final paragraphs keep both the desire to watch and the intention to finish.

exercises.prompt: What would the writer prefer if an unexpected event made the deadline impossible?
options: Consult the other person early instead of silently being late
Treat every promise as impossible to change
Wait until Monday without saying anything
exercises.explain: The final paragraph recommends early consultation, while distinguishing this occasion when completion was feasible.

grammar: inference corrected by わけではない
obligation and negative polarity with わけにはいかない
watch.prompt: Optionally read or watch a scene from your own media in which someone gives advice or refuses an invitation. Identify the listener and reason; decide what is suggested, what is denied and what must still be done.
